title: Choose and name columns

outcomes.can: Compute a column and give it a name.
Build a text column from other columns.
Say where a column's new name can and cannot be used.

intro: The SELECT list decides what each result row contains. It can hold columns, calculations and joined text, and every one of them can be given a clear name. This module also covers returning each distinct value once.

steps.title: Columns can be computed
steps.text: Each item in the SELECT list produces one column of the result, worked out separately for every row. An item can be a column, or an expression such as budget / 12. +, -, * and / work on numbers. ROUND(value, 2) rounds to two decimal places. The || operator joins pieces of text, and text you type yourself goes in single quotes, as in first_name || ' ' || last_name. AS gives a result column a name: budget / 12 AS monthly_budget. A computed column without a name is shown as ?column?, which tells a reader nothing, so always name them. AS changes only the result. The table is not changed.

steps.title: Predict the header
steps.text: Read the SELECT list and predict the first line of the result.

steps.title: Follow one row
steps.text: The header shows the new names: department and monthly_budget. For the Sales row, budget is 1100000.00. Divided by 12 and rounded to two places that is 91666.67. Every row is worked out the same way, from its own budget.

steps.title: Use a new name too early
steps.text: The second item uses the name the first item was just given. Read the example before checking.

steps.title: Read the error
steps.text: Check the example. Error 42703 says column "monthly" does not exist. A name given with AS belongs to the result, and the other items in the same SELECT list cannot see it. Repeat the expression instead: budget / 12 * 2.

steps.title: Each value once
steps.text: SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicate rows from the result. With one column, each value appears once. With several columns, DISTINCT looks at the whole row, so a row is dropped only when every column matches another row.

steps.title: Count the distinct values
steps.text: Six departments share a few locations. Predict how many rows come back.

steps.title: Name a computed column
steps.text: The starter computes the right values but leaves the column without a name.

steps.title: Build a full name
steps.text: Work from the prompt. Mind the space between the two names.

questions.prompt: What is the first line of the result?

choices.feedback: AS gave both columns new names, and the header shows them.
Both columns were renamed with AS, so the original names are not shown.
The computed column was given the name monthly_budget.

questions.prompt: What happens when you check this example?

choices.text: It returns monthly and a second column twice as large.
choices.feedback: The second item cannot see the name monthly, so the statement fails.

choices.text: PostgreSQL reports an error on line 1.
choices.feedback: monthly is a name for a result column. Items in the same SELECT list cannot use it (42703).

choices.text: It returns one column, because the second is ignored.
choices.feedback: A bad name is an error. Nothing is ignored, and nothing is returned.
DISTINCT removes the repeats, and several departments share a location.
DISTINCT keeps one row for each different value, not one row in total.
The departments are in Denver, Chicago and Austin, and each appears once.

review.evidence: Open a fresh starter on a later visit, with the earlier answer closed. A first unaided pass on every case is later evidence of the skill. A hinted pass stays recorded as assisted.

drillGap: These drills practise one SELECT feature each. They do not combine a computed column with a required name.
